text: How does a distributed-feedback (DFB) laser achieve single-frequency operation?
choices: By using an extremely short cavity so that only one longitudinal mode fits in the gain band
By cooling the device to cryogenic temperatures
By incorporating a Bragg grating (typically with a quarter-wave phase shift) that provides wavelength-selective feedback
By using two independent gain media at different wavelengths
explanation: A DFB laser embeds a Bragg grating (Λ = mλ_B/2n_eff) along the cavity; a quarter-wave phase shift selects a single mode at the stopband center, giving SMSR > 40 dB. The short-cavity single-mode mechanism describes a VCSEL, not a DFB, and cryogenic cooling or dual gain media are not how DFBs select a mode.
